title: Wild Wings in the Woods and Inside Sauter-Finegan
summary: Percussion pieces and small-band record that RCA requested.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: favorite things that I heard from the Sauter-Finegan record is that woodwind thing that you did, "Wild Wings in the Woods."
That's one of mine too. Well done, that thing. There's another one in there I like, "10,000 B.C." That was a tune in a musical I did.
Which is kind of a percussion piece.
Percussion and singer. There were lyrics to that originally, which I couldn't use. It was from a musical called the Reluctant Virgin.
Especially on the one record, Inside Sauter-Finegan, at least half of the things on the record weren't with the full band.
That was asked for by Victor.
Travis playing, "How About You" with the rhythm section.

That's right. We used to do a lot of things like that on the raod, but this sort of kicked it off. They asked us to make a small band record, because critics loved small bands, in those days particularly. I think the critics pushed this way and that's one of the reasons for the rise of rock; that's one reason, there are others. They didn't like the big bands; they still don't. They'd been castigated and Harvey Estern (phonetic spelling) had use of the library for the rehearsal band at the YMHA, and the bigness of the band there (inaudible). It might be too much for some people, but anyway, we did it because RCA asked us to, and the other part of it was that on the road after playing all night, the smallness is welcomed. We used to feel a sense of relief from
doing that. Another one I like in there was "Eddie and the Witch Doctor". I don't know where these names came about.
That was percussion; that was Moussey's piece.
The notes for all of those records, you and Bill, I guess wrote them, and they were very funny with a very dry sense of humor.
I'm glad you got that. One of the things I tried to get into those notes, is the respect of the people.
I wanted it that way; I hope that came across.
